article_text:
Zwei Männer sollen mutmaßlich mit Einbruchswerkzeug im Innenhof des Dresdner Zwingers unterwegs gewesen sein. Die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen wurden deshalb verstärkt

Nach einem mutmaßlichen Einbruchversuch im Dresdner Zwinger sind die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen verstärkt worden. Nach Angaben der Staatlichen Kunstsammlungen Dresden (SKD) sind darin die Polizeidirektion Dresden und der Sicherheitsdienst der SKD eingebunden. Sicherheit habe oberste Priorität. "Alle bestehenden Maßnahmen werden laufend überprüft und regelmäßig an die Sicherheitslagen angepasst sowie weiter verbessert", hieß es.

Wie die Staatsanwaltschaft Dresden und das Landeskriminalamt mitteilten, hatte ein Mitarbeiter des Sicherheitsdienstes am Dienstagmorgen im Innenraum des Dresdner Zwingers zwei Männer angetroffen, die wahrscheinlich Einbruchswerkzeug bei sich hatten. Als er das Duo ansprach, flohen die Männer in unbekannte Richtung. Die Ermittler gehen von einem versuchten Einbruch in die Porzellansammlung aus und bitten Zeugen um Hinweise.

Im Zwinger befinden sich mit dem Mathematisch-Physikalischen Salon, der Porzellansammlung und der Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister mit der Skulpturensammlung bis 1800 berühmte Sammlungen. «Die Sicherheit für diese herausragenden Schätze hat größte Bedeutung. Dem tragen wir unter anderem mit der sichtbaren Präsenz durch unser Wachschutzunternehmen Rechnung», sagte eine SKD-Sprecherin. Das rechtzeitige Agieren des Sicherheitspersonals zeige, wie wichtig und zugleich wirkungsvoll diese Maßnahmen seien.

Hackerangriff auf die SKD im Januar

Ende Januar hatten die SKD über einen Hackerangriff informiert. Später berichteten Medien darüber, dass es Diebe auf eine wertvolle Schale und eine Vase aus China abgesehen hatten. "Konkrete Anhaltspunkte für einen sachlichen Zusammenhang des versuchten Einbruchs mit dem Cyberangriff im Januar 2026 liegen bislang nicht vor", teilte die Staatsanwaltschaft mit.

2019 war die Schatzkammer Grünes Gewölbe Schauplatz eines dreisten Einbruchs und Diebstahls. Die Täter erbeuteten Juwelen von unschätzbarem Wert und wurden von einem Gericht zu Haftstrafen verurteilt.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在本周的《银幕》播客节目中，团队深入探讨了拉开颁奖季序幕的各大核心热议话题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "请在上方观看或在下方收听", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "主持温迪·米切尔（Wendy Mitchell）与颁奖及票房编辑查尔斯（Charles）一同探讨了内森·菲尔德（Nathan Fielder）与兰斯·奥本海姆（Lance Oppenheim）的纪录片《万物皆可窥》如何引爆颁奖季，并迅速成为一名强有力的竞争者。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我认为作为一名投票者，你会感到有点兴奋，就像如果你投票支持那部电影，你就是在拥抱先锋电影一样，”查尔斯说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "两人还剖析了最佳影片竞争中正在涌现的其他电影、非英语电影的前景，以及身兼多片竞争者的桑德拉·惠勒（Sandra Huller）和罗伯特·帕丁森（Robert Pattinson）最终将凭借哪几部作品获得提名。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“（帕丁森）赢得并值得我们的尊重，因为他在利用自己的影响力去促成那些极其有趣的电影拍摄，而不是拍很多千篇一律的大片，”甘特（Gant）说。“而且即使他出演一部大型漫画改编电影，他也会带来一部真正有趣的电影和真正精彩的表演。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如需下载或订阅未来的节目，请搜索“The Screen Podcast”，该节目已在 Apple Podcasts、Spotify、Acast 和 YouTube 上线。", "links": [{"text": "Apple Podcasts", "url": "https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/the-screen-international-podcast/id1486784949"}, {"text": "Spotify", "url": "https://open.spotify.com/show/5J0Y9mmPCUOHNMUQDxc7dK?si=jz20RqTaSiWoogJcICOMYA&nd=1"}, {"text": "Acast", "url": "https://feeds.acast.com/public/shows/6a4cf2b47c0256f6394e534e"}, {"text": "YouTube", "url": "https://www.youtube.com/@ScreenInternational"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《银幕》播客由艾莉·卡尔南（Ellie Calnan）制作，温迪·米切尔担任主编。每周四更新新节目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "来自《银幕》播客的更多内容", "links": [{"text": "More from The Screen Podcast", "url": "https://www.screendaily.com/the-screen-podcast/12264.subject"}], "translated": true}]

article_text:
On this week’s episode of The Screen Podcast, the team delves into the biggest talking points kicking off awards season.

Watch above or listen below

Host Wendy Mitchell is joined by awards and box office editor Charles to discuss how Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything has exploded the awards race, quickly becoming a top contender.

“I think that as a voter, you get to feel a little bit excited, like you’re embracing vanguard cinema if you vote for that film,” Charles said.

The duo also unpack what other films are emerging in the best picture race, how non-English-language films will fare and which performances will multi-contenders Sandra Huller and Robert Pattinson ultimately nab a nomination for.

“[Pattinson] commands and deserves our respect because he is using his power to help get made fantastically interesting films rather than a lot of generic blockbuster fair,” Gant said. “And even when he does a big comic-book film, he does a really interesting film and a really interesting performance.”

To download or subscribe to future episodes, search for ‘The Screen Podcast’, which is available on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , Acast and YouTube .

The Screen Podcast is produced by Ellie Calnan, with Wendy Mitchell serving as editorial director. New episodes every Thursday.

オランダの写真家ヘラルト・ペトルス・フィーレット（Gerard Petrus Fieret、1924〜2009）の展覧会「Raw Art on Paper by G.P. Fieret」が、2026年11月13日（金）から12月27日（日）まで、東京・恵比寿のPOSTで開催される。1965年から1975年に制作されたヴィンテージプリント36点を紹介する。

フィーレットは、オランダ・ハーグ生まれの写真家。詩やデッサンにも取り組みながら、1965年から約10年間、写真制作に没頭した。プラクチカの一眼レフを手に街を歩き、若い女性や路上で遊ぶ子どもたち、動物、自身の姿など、日常の光景を撮影。現像からプリントまで自ら手がけた。

その作品を特徴づけるのは、荒い粒子やピンボケ、露出過多、ソラリゼーションなど、一般的には写真の「失敗」とされる要素だ。さらに、作品の無断使用を警戒し、プリントの表面に自身の署名や著作権スタンプを繰り返し押した。なかには同じプリントに7回もスタンプが押されたものもあり、その痕跡自体が作品の一部となっている。

生前は写真界の周縁に位置していたが、没後に再評価が進み、2016年にはパリのル・バルで回顧展が開催された。現在では、戦後オランダ写真を代表する作家のひとりとして、アウトサイダー・アートの文脈からも注目されている。

本展は、2026年にVan Zoetendaal Publishersから刊行された同名写真集に合わせて企画されたもの。会場では、ゼラチンシルバープリントならではの紙の質感や、スタンプのインクの濃淡、作家の手仕事の痕跡を間近で鑑賞できる。また、写真集『Raw Art on Paper by G.P. Fieret』に加え、編者ウィレム・ファン・ズーテンダールがデザインしたポスター4種、ポストカード15種も販売される。

article_text:
⁠Jurandir Filho ⁠, ⁠ Rogério Montanare ⁠ e ⁠ Thiago Siqueira ⁠⁠ conversam sobre quando a gente era criança nos anos 80/90 e a televisão brasileira não tinha limites! Crescemos assistindo a filmes que, definitivamente, não eram feitos para crianças! E o mais absurdo? Muitos passavam em plena luz do dia, na Sessão da Tarde, no Cinema em Casa e em outras sessões da TV aberta! “Rambo”, “RoboCop”, “Comando para Matar”, “Brinquedo Assassino”, “Sexta-Feira 13”, “A Hora do Pesadelo”… Violência, sangue, mortes e traumas de infância! E não podemos esquecer das comédias repletas de nudez e piadas adultas, como “Porky’s”, “O Último Americano Virgem” e tantos outros filmes que assistíamos sem entender metade do que estava acontecendo!

Neste RapaduraCast, abrimos o baú das memórias proibidas e relembramos os filmes que marcaram nossa infância, mesmo quando a gente não tinha idade para estar na frente da televisão! Como essas produções chegavam tão facilmente até nós? Será que nossos pais sabiam o que estávamos assistindo? E, principalmente, como esses filmes influenciaram toda uma geração? ⁠

article_text:
News

Shuttering Early, Art Basel Paris Also Removes Public Sculptures

Works by Simone Fattal, Manfred Pernice, and Niki de Saint Phalle are among those that will be removed early from Winston Churchill Avenue ahead of the fair’s early closure.

Following the news that Art Basel Paris will close early on October 23 , all outdoor sculptures installed on Winston Churchill Avenue outside the Grand Palais for the fair's accompanying public program will be dismantled as early as tonight, October 22.

The main program of Art Basel Paris will end two days early on Friday at 7pm, after the fair's first and now only public day, due to "potential demonstrations across Paris this weekend and in the interest of safeguarding our visitors," organizers told exhibitors in an email sent out today.

The fair's public program on Winston Churchill Avenue was scheduled to run from October 21–25, and features works from Simone Fattal, Carmen Herrera, Marcello Maloberti, Keita Miyazaki, Manfred Pernice, Niki de Saint Phalle, and Yinka Shonibare.

"Unfortunately, only on view today and tomorrow, as it has to be dismantled, along with other sculptures, because of the announced riots and people who simply want to resort to violence," Kwade wrote in a statement posted to Instagram , stating that her nearly 15-foot sculpture, "L’Élévation des Mondes" (2026) , would be taken down on Friday. "Protest is good, but why everything has to be smashed and destroyed is beyond ……It certainly doesn’t help the cause."

In a later statement to Hyperallergic , Kwade clarified that she wanted the work to stay in place but, following a discussion with the fair organizers, it was jointly decided that the work would be removed early.

"I strongly support the legitimate concerns behind these protests, particularly the demands for better education, social justice and fair living conditions," Kwade stated. "It is therefore especially sad to see these important causes overshadowed by violence and destruction, which ultimately undermine the very issues people are fighting for."

Galleria Raffaella Cortese in Milan further confirmed that Maloberti's "CIEL" (2026) is scheduled for dismantling tonight, and gallery rosenfeld in London told Hyperallergic that Miyazaki's "A Symbiotic Form" (2025) would be coming down on Friday. The information page about the eight sculptures on Winston Churchill Avenue was also removed today.

"The Public Program spans several sites with different operating conditions, so arrangements are being assessed site by site," an Art Basel spokesperson told Hyperallergic . "Works presented on Avenue Winston Churchill will be removed shortly in coordination with the relevant parties. We will share further information on the remaining sites once arrangements are confirmed."

Other artworks for the public program span Clemenceau Place, the Cité de l’Architecture et du Patrimoine, Jean Perrin Square, the Petit Palais, and other public grounds around Paris.

After the Grand Palais went into temporary lockdown during the Art Basel Paris installation amid nearby protests, event organizers initially proceeded with the fair's original schedule. When they announced the fair's early closure earlier today, October 22, they cited the demonstrations surrounding the month-long nationwide campaign over France’s declining education system and public services. Police have used violent tactics on protesters in demonstrations so far, from inflicting violent injuries on teenagers to tear-gassing elected officials such as Mayor Bally Bagayoko and Deputy Mayor Landry Ngang of Saint-Denis.

Ahead of this weekend's protests, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu also stated that military forces from the terrorist defense mission Operation Sentinelle will be deployed over the weekend to control protesters in a "massive" security operation.
excerpt_original: Works by Simone Fattal, Manfred Pernice, and Niki de Saint Phalle are among those that will be removed early from Winston Churchill Avenue ahead of the fair’s early closure.

article_text:
建築家・石上純也が第1回「バラガン賞」を受賞。ボッテガ・ヴェネタがメキシコで祝賀イベントを開催

建築 家・ 石上純也 が、建築の可能性を切り拓く人物を顕彰する国際建築賞「バラガン賞」の初代受賞者に選ばれた。10月9日には、 ルイス・バラガン が手がけた メキシコシティ の歴史的建築「ラ・クアドラ」で授賞式が開催され、 ボッテガ・ヴェネタ が受賞を祝う記念ランチを共催した。

建築 家の 石上純也 が、新たに創設された国際建築賞「バラガン賞（The Barragán Prize）」の第1回受賞者に選ばれた。10月9日、 メキシコシティ にある ルイス・バラガン 建築「ラ・クアドラ（La Cuadra）」で授賞式が開催され、 イタリア のラグジュアリーブランド、 ボッテガ・ヴェネタ が受賞を祝うランチイベントを共催した。

バラガン賞は、メキシコ人建築家として唯一 プリツカー賞 を受賞したルイス・バラガンの名を冠した国際建築賞。既成概念にとらわれず、建築の可能性を拡張し、人々の暮らしや世界との関わり方に新たな視点をもたらす人物を顕彰することを目的としている。

初回の会場となったラ・クアドラは、バラガンが1960年代後半に設計した邸宅兼厩舎で、20世紀メキシコ建築を代表する作品のひとつ。光や色彩、水、庭園を巧みに取り込み、建築と自然の関係を探究したバラガンの思想を体現する場所だ。

一方、今回初代受賞者に選ばれた石上もまた、建築と自然の関係を独自の視点から問い直してきた建築家だ。東京藝術大学大学院修了後、妹島和世建築設計事務所を経て、2004年に自身の建築設計事務所を設立した。

代表作のひとつである神奈川工科大学の《KAIT工房》（2008年）では、林立する細い柱によって、建物の内部に森のような空間を創出。栃木県那須町の《水庭》（2018年）では、318本の樹木を移植し、160の池を配置することで、自然と人工の境界を曖昧にする風景を生み出した。また、 ロンドン の《 サーペンタイン・パビリオン 2019》では、石板を重ねた屋根が地面から立ち上がるような構造を実現するなど、建築を建物という枠組みから解き放つ試みを続けている。

2010年には第12回 ヴェネチア・ビエンナーレ 国際建築展で金獅子賞を受賞。2018年には パリ の カルティエ 現代美術財団で大規模個展「Junya Ishigami, Freeing Architecture」が開催されるなど、その活動は建築と現代美術の領域を横断して国際的な注目を集めてきた。2019年にはオーベル賞、2024年にはフレデリック・キースラー建築芸術賞を受賞している。

授賞式に合わせて開催された記念ランチは、 ボッテガ・ヴェネタ と同ブランドのクリエイティブ・ディレクター、ルイーズ・トロッターが、メキシコ出身の建築家フェルナンド・ロメロとともに主催。アーティストの マリーナ・アブラモヴィッチ やペドロ・レイエス、建築家のベネデッタ・タリアブーエ、ユルゲン・マイヤー・H、レイモンド・ライアン、駐メキシコ日本国特命全権大使の本清耕造らが出席し、石上の受賞を祝福した。

ボッテガ・ヴェネタは、建築、アート、 デザイン を横断する創造的な活動を支援するべく、今回のバラガン賞創設に際してラ・クアドラとパートナーシップを締結している。

article_text:
そごう美術館（横浜市）で「KIRIKANE Sculpture 山本茜」が12月6日まで開催されています。仏像や仏画の装飾技法として受け継がれてきた「截金（きりかね）」とガラスを組み合わせた「截金ガラス」という独自の表現で注目を集める山本茜さんの、美術館では初の個展です。展示室に足を踏み入れると、まずは本展で初公開の最新作《源氏物語シリーズ第十八帖「松風」―浮木舟―》がお出迎え。ガラスの色のグラデーションと截金の波や松の文様が織りなす、幻想的な美の世界に一気に引き込まれました。

『源氏物語』シリーズが一堂に

本展では、初めて手がけた截金ガラス作品から最新作まで、約60点が集結しています。中でも、ライフワークとして取り組み続けてきた『源氏物語』シリーズが一堂に集う空間に圧倒されました。ガラスの中に浮かび上がる繊細で優美な情景――。次から次へと目移りします。作品の周りをぐるりと回ったり、上からのぞき込んだり……と角度を変えると、截金の輝きや色など、作品が見せる表情の移ろいを楽しむことができます。

「中学の古典の授業で『源氏物語』に出会って以来、その世界に惹かれ、ここまで導かれてきた」という山本さん。「『源氏物語』を自分なりの表現で絵巻にしたい」と京都市立芸術大学で日本画を学ぶ中、「截金」の技法に出会います。重要無形文化財「截金」保持者である江里佐代子さん（1945～2007年）のもとで技法を修得した後、「截金を装飾ではなく表現そのものとしてガラスの中に浮遊させたい」と考え、富山ガラス造形研究所でガラス技術の研鑽を積みました。そして、ついに第一号の実験作ができたとき、「源氏物語54帖のイメージがザーっと”降ってきた”」そうです。以来、独自の技法を磨きながら、実現可能なイメージから順に作品にしてきたといいます。展示室では、『源氏物語』シリーズが制作順に並んでいるので、山本さんの歩みもたどることができます。

制作工程にも注目

工房の写真や手製の道具、失敗作など制作工程も惜しみなく披露されています。こちらも見逃せません。

江里佐代子さんの「道具の貸し借りをしてはいけない」という教えに従い、研磨ガラスや研磨台などの道具はすべて手作りです。制作図面は、数学や物理の知識も駆使した緻密な計算のうえで作品の情景が構築されていることを物語り、さらに驚嘆させられます。

また最新作《源氏物語シリーズ第十八帖「松風」―浮木舟―》は、完成までに通算52回の窯入れと4年の歳月を費やしたといいます。雅で涼やかな作品世界の裏には、想像もつかないような「格闘」があるのです。

これまでの展覧会で山本さんの作品に出会い、「もっとたくさん見たい！」と熱望したファンも多いでしょう。その願いがようやく叶います。「KIRIKANE Sculpture 山本茜」はそごう美術館（横浜）で10月24日から12月6日まで。ぜひお見逃しなく。

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班・美間実沙）

article_text:
1. Introduction

Greetings.

Welcome to the Do Ho Suh exhibition at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea.

With works found in cities around the world, including Seoul, New York, and London, Do Ho Suh is well established as a leading South Korean installation artist.

This large-scale solo exhibition explores Suh’s artistic practice, shaped by his distinctive visual language over the past three decades.

For this artist who grew up in Seoul but has mainly worked abroad, personal movement has been a process through which different cultures, languages, systems, and communities have intersected, collided, and overlapped. For Suh, a home is not merely a fixed building set in a specific place. It is a sensory space that moves with the body, carries memories around the world, and connects a person’s experiences with those of others. His conception of home is not something unique to those who cross borders, like Suh. Every day that we open our doors and step outside, we, too, become nomads as we leave the familiar behind and adapt to a different world. Suh’s work has a universal resonance, and he is internationally recognized among the prominent artists of our time.

This exhibition includes previously unseen early works and drawings. They offer a glimpse into the questions he explored and the experiments he performed at the beginning of his career, while also demonstrating his playful imagination. The exhibition presents a broad selection of Suh’s works, including some of his most recent pieces, as it traces how his ideas have shifted and expanded over the last thirty years. It is hoped that it will prove to be another milestone along Suh’s journey as an artist who continues to evolve and create. It is also hoped that it will become a space where our questions intersect and intertwine with each other’s and, ideally, a home where the memories and questions of each of us can linger.

The works in this exhibition are not organized according to theme. Instead, the exhibition arranges the early and later works, drawings, and installations to reflect on and expand upon the concepts of home and the body and of space and time within a cohesive context. As you move through the web of relationships Suh has woven among these concepts, you can take a moment to add your own memories and experiences to what you encounter.

This year, that honor goes to Gagosian for its immaculately produced ode to René Magritte and his sprawling influence. The smash-hit show has received some 10,000 visitors since opening September 24, with lines often stretching around the block.", "links": [{"text": "ode", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/art-world/gagosian-plots-blockbuster-magritte-show-in-london-2789545"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://news.artnet.com/app/news-upload/2026/10/MAGRI_1961.0001_CRP-1-1-1024x699.jpg", "alt": "a painting that in its top half appears to be daytime with blue skies and clouds but below seems to be a house shown at night with its lighits on and the mysterious silhouette of a man in a hat looking at the horizon, we can see him from behind", "caption": "", "credit": "Artnet News"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "René Magritte, The Empire of Light (1961). article_text:
When Frieze Week arrives in London, there is always one exhibition that you’d be embarrassed to admit you missed. This year, that honor goes to Gagosian for its immaculately produced ode to René Magritte and his sprawling influence. The smash-hit show has received some 10,000 visitors since opening September 24, with lines often stretching around the block.

René Magritte, The Empire of Light (1961). Photo: Prudence Cuming Associates Ltd, Heidi Horten Collection, © 2026 ADAGP, Paris and DACS, London.

Featuring a whopping 120 works by the Surrealist master and 45 of contemporary art’s biggest names—including Jeff Koons , Glenn Ligon , Jordan Wolfson , and Issy Wood —” This Is Still Not a Pipe: The Afterlife of Magritte ,” through December 12, was always going to be big deal. Less predictable is how the show captures a prevailing mood. It stuck in my head, its themes and motifs reverberating throughout a recent gallery hop in Mayfair and East London. Again and again, I was reminded of what seems to be the Gagosian show’s central thesis: that a once-novel strain of Surrealism is now the dominant artistic lens on our world.

Here are just a few of the surprising parallels I encountered.

Impossibility

Nicole Eisenman, The Waiter (2026). Image: Katie Morrison, © Nicole Eisenman, courtesy the artist and Sadie Coles HQ, London.

Just a few streets from Gagosian, an exhibition of 10 new works by Nicole Eisenman at Sadie Coles (through November 21) offered the same incongruity that characterizes many Magritte masterpieces. The Waiter (2026) is an epic, 11-by-21-foot spectacle in which high-definition planets and swirling galaxies float above the lichen-covered slabs of Stonehenge . The kicker is the lone figure of a waiter, his shirt collar open and bowtie limp as though at the end of his shift. What is he doing there? The man gazes up, as confused by the cosmos as we are by his impossibly mundane presence within it.

From left to right: René Magritte, Pictorial Content (1947). Photo: Margaret Carrigan. Nicole Eisenman, Parking Lot of Violent Forces and Depressive Positions (2026). Image: Katie Morrison, © Nicole Eisenman, courtesy the Artist and Sadie Coles HQ, London..

The empty, flat expanse of Magritte paintings like The Flowers of the Journey (1926) and The Leader of the Band (1955) takes on new meaning in Eisenman’s Parking Lot of Violent Forces and Depressive Positions (2026). The effect is ominous, yes, but also absurd, infusing irony into the Philip Guston -style satire, in which ICE agents pile into a clown car to patrol the desolate, gray surrounds of a strip mall. A monstrous, dripping figure, apparently composed of exhaust fumes, brings to mind the same oozing forms found in Magritte’s Pictorial Content (1947), one of the cruder images he made during his short-lived vache period.

Ambiguity

From left to right: René Magritte, The Commonplace (1964) Image: © 2026 ADAGP, Paris and DACS, London. Louis Fratino, Summer in the city (2026). Image: Kerry McFate, © Louis Fratino, courtesy David Zwirner.

Distorted spatial logic gives a claustrophobic feel to the canvases of Louis Fratino , who has prepared 12 new paintings for “ Prose ” at David Zwirner , through October 31. Summer in the City (2026) uses an unusual vantage point to divide the picture plane, layering the disparate lives of urban strangers and leaving its central figure as dislocated as the one in Magritte’s The Commonplace (1964).

From left to right: Louis Fratino, The green bath (2026). Photo: Kerry McFate, © Louis Fratino, courtesy David Zwirner. Victor Man, Titiriteros (2023). Image: def image, © Victor Man, courtesy Gagosian.

Fratino’s running interest in everyday domesticity turns a little sickly in The green bath (2026), where two languid nudes sit entwined. It is impossible not to think of the similarly emerald-tinged palette preferred by Salman Toor , who is having his solo European museum debut at the Courtauld , until January 10. His paintings seduce us into a dreamy otherworld, filled with queer intimacies that have too often been pushed into the shadows. A more sinister comparison is Titiriteros (2023) by the ever-mysterious Victor Man , included in the Gagosian survey. Glowing lime green and with all the moody atmosphere of an El Greco , it closes in on three women burning a piece of paper that bears the artist’s initials. As in Fratino’s painting, expressionless faces and averted eyes leave the viewer guessing as to the composition’s true meaning.

Reinvention

From left to right: René Magritte, The Triumphant March (1948). Image: © 2026 ADAGP, Paris and DACS, London, courtesy Brachot Gallery. M: Alex Da Corte, Slow Graffiti (2017). Image: Joseph Hu, © Alex Da Corte, courtesy the Artist and Sadie Coles HQ, London. R: Installation view of Adam Lewis Jacob’s “Short Vamps for Long Wear” at Neven, 2026. Image: Dominique Croshaw, courtesy of the artist and Neven, London.

Vast, central podiums filling the main rooms of the Gagosian show are not to be overlooked. Many of the smaller objects assembled call for close examination, as is the case with Alex da Corte ‘s Slow Graffiti (2017). Sexualized objects like the high-heeled shoe have long held a fetishistic appeal for the Surrealists, and Da Corte’s mini, winged stiletto installation flattens the distinction between real life and fantasy.

In Magritte’s The Triumphal March (1948), meanwhile, a disembodied calf in a high-heeled shoe gains a life of its own while donning pieces of fancy dress. At Neven gallery in Bethnal Green, Adam Lewis Jacob has broken apart used stilettos to build wacky new constructions that still contain telling signifiers of their former life for his show “ Short Vamps for Long Wear ,” until October 24.

Doubling

From left to right: Charlotte Kingsnorth, Marshmallow Bench (2026). Image: Jack Elliot Edwards, courtesy the artist and Rose Easton, London. R: Sarah Lucas, SLAG (2022). Image: Steve Russell Studios, © Sarah Lucas, courtesy Sadie Coles HQ, London.

A short walk away, at Rose Easton , the group show “ Lumps and Bumps ” was inspired by the Comme des Garçons Spring/Summer 1997 collection “Body Meets Dress, Dress Meets Body,” but has plenty of incidental callbacks to the Magritte survey. Through December 12, it features the newly commissioned Marshmallow Bench by Charlotte Kingsnorth , a plump, pink leather sofa with an uncomfortably corporeal quality.

For Magritte, too, the body can double as an object, as in works from the Gagosian show like The Music Lesson (1965), in which an ear is attached to a bell, and The Red Model (1935), in which shoes become feet. In his The Art of Living (1967), a head balloons, becoming ridiculously oversized. A similar lack of constraint governs the slumped, stuffed figure, its bulging seams all awry, in Sarah Lucas ‘s SLAG (2022), also included in the show.

The Gagosian survey’s oldest work dates to 1926, exactly one century ago, but many of the later pieces were made in the past five years. If Magritte’s influence has undoubtedly endured through the decades, my recent gallery hop left me with the sense that his eye for the enigmatic and absurd is more relevant now than ever.

article_text:
安全対策に疑問の声──ライト旧邸での死亡事故、元従業員は「屋根から物が外れるのを2度目撃」

フランク・ロイド・ライト の旧居タリアセン・ウエストで起きた死亡事故を受け、維持管理や安全対策に疑問の声が上がっている。元従業員は過去にも屋根から部材が外れるのを目撃したと証言した。

アメリカ ・アリゾナ州スコッツデールにある 建築 家 フランク・ロイド・ライト （1867–1959）の旧居兼アトリエ、タリアセン・ウエストで10月16日、強風で外れたアクリル製の屋根部材が見学者に当たり、死亡する事故が起きた。これを受け、施設の維持管理や安全対策に疑問の声が上がっている。

スコッツデール警察によると、亡くなったのはブラジルのパラナ教皇庁立カトリック大学学長、ロジェリオ・レナト・マテウッチ（55歳）。大学幹部向けの国際プログラムに参加するため、アリゾナ州立大学を訪れていた。事故は施設内を歩いて巡る見学ツアーの途中に起き、現場で死亡が確認された。

米国立気象局によると、当日のスコッツデール周辺では時速約35キロの東風が吹き、最大時速約51キロの突風が観測されていたという。周辺地域には強風注意報が出され、移動や安全に支障が生じる恐れがあるとして警戒が呼びかけられていた。

施設を運営するフランク・ロイド・ライト財団のCEO、ジョー・スペクターは声明で、「亡くなられた方のご家族と親しい方々に、心よりお悔やみ申し上げます」と表明。「プライバシーを尊重し、当局が調査を完了できるよう、これ以上の詳細は公表しません」とした。当局は気象条件に起因する事故とみて、調査を進めている。

@USATODAY

一方、事故から数日がたつなかで、安全対策によって防げたのではないかという疑問も浮上している。

ともにアリゾナを訪れていた同大学の副学長、ヴィダル・マルティンスは、地元紙 アリゾナ・リパブリック に対し、「一般に公開されている場所なのですから、安全対策を講じる必要があります」と語った。マルティンスは見学ツアーには参加しておらず、事故の知らせを受けて現場に向かい、当局が立ち入りを規制していた区域でマテウッチの遺体を見たという。同紙には、敷地内の岩や砂漠の植物の間に半透明のパネルが落ちている写真も提供した。マルティンスによると、このパネルがマテウッチに当たった部材とみられる。

元従業員も、施設の安全性に懸念を示している。匿名を条件に地元テレビ局 AZファミリー の取材に応じ、在職中の6カ月間に、屋根から物が外れるのを2度目撃したと証言した。また、7月のモンスーンに伴う荒天時には、同様の透明なパネルが風で揺れ、外れかける様子を撮影していたという。「建物の安全を確保するために必要なところへ資金が適切に回されているとは思えません」と訴えた。

アリゾナ・リパブリックは財団に対し、屋根の点検や強風への対策、再開の見通しについて質問したが、財団が示した声明は点検や安全対策には触れていなかった。施設は現在も一般公開を停止しており、再開日は決まっていない。

タリアセン・ウエストは、ライトが1937年に建設に着手し、1959年に亡くなるまで冬の住まい兼アトリエとして使用した。かつてはフランク・ロイド・ライト建築学校の教育拠点でもあった。同校はその後、ザ・スクール・オブ・アーキテクチャー（The School of Architecture）に改称し、現在はスコッツデール市内の別の場所で教育活動を続けている。タリアセン・ウエストはフランク・ロイド・ライト財団の本部となり、見学ツアーや展示、教育プログラムを通じてライトの建築を伝える施設として一般公開されていた。（翻訳：編集部）

article_text:
Retenu captif par une étrange famille, Tommy n’a d’autre choix de distraction que de lire Aldous Huxley et Ray Bradbury. Jan Komasa donne ainsi un indice sur son film, qui abandonne le réalisme pour devenir une dissertation allégorique aux frontières du genre. D’un côté, un lad anglais, adepte de nuits d’ivresse et d’accès de violence qu’il filme et diffuse sur les réseaux sociaux.

De l’autre, une famille au fascisme intime qui le séquestre et lui ajuste la laisse. Ce septième film du réalisateur de La Communion (2020) fait du foyer un monde miniature, où la surveillance tient lieu de marque d’attention. Chris, « bon père de famille », incarné par Stephen Graham, semble vouloir corriger toute une génération à travers l’exemple de ce garçon. Achevé juste avant le tournage d’ Adolescence, The Good Boy se place dans son sillage sans en être l’antidote.

Au père en larmes, culpabilisant de n’avoir su préserver son fils du masculinisme, répond ici un patriarche convaincu des vertus du violent serrage de vis. Face à Graham, le comédien Anson Boon, fascinante tête à claques qui jouait Johnny Rotten dans Pistol de Danny Boyle, côtoie Andrea Riseborough en mère spectrale. Tous nous entraînent dans un conte politique maximaliste, sans morale, où l’autorité se croit aimante et où la soumission offre un certain confort.

The Good Boy de Jan Komasa, sortie le 11 novembre, CutCutCut/Sooner (1 h 50)

article_text:
Films and events

Thrill

Josephine

Winner of the Grand Jury Dramatic Prize at Sundance, this suspenseful and devastating film follows a child trying to navigate life after witnessing a sexual assault.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Beth de Araújo

With Mason Reeves, Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan

USA 2026. 119min

Courtesy of Curzon

Language English

Certificate BBFC18

Introduction

Eight-year-old Josephine (an astounding performance by newcomer Mason Reeves) knows that she saw something bad, but struggles to find answers. Her parents (a brilliant Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) grapple with how to comfort her. Weaving thriller and horror conventions within a serious and sobering scenario, Beth de Araújo creates an often uncomfortable yet vital film that interrogates how we explain the unspeakable.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, sex, and sexual violence.

Contains flashing images.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Girl Unknown

Jing Zou’s captivating debut feature, an intimate, decade-spanning character study, explores the consequences of the single-child policy on generations of Chinese girls.

Prima Facie

Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo gives a captivating central performance in Susanna White’s much-anticipated screen adaptation of Suzie Miller’s globally acclaimed play.

The Liberation

In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader.

article_text:
NatGeo’s Everest: The Other Side by Oscar-winning documentary filmmakers Jimmy Chin and Chai Vasarhelyi and Independent Film Company’s psychological horror Breeder are specialty debuts, along Greenwich Entertainment’s Queen At Sea , and docs Who Killed Alex Odeh? , Paging Hezbollah (by the director of Am I A Racist ?) and Heathens .

Briarcliff’s holiday horror-comedy Christmas At The Kringles and Sight & Sound Presents: Joshua Live! from Roadside Attractions are the indie – and the only – new wide releases with Halloween falling on a Saturday this year.

Following La Bola Negra , Netflix debuts its second official box office entry, Peter Berg’s war drama The Mosquito Bowl ( see Deadline review ). Sony Pictures Classics jumps to 1,112 screens with The Only Living Pickpocket in New York starring Gotham Award-nominated John Turturro. And coming off two Gotham nominations of its own this week, Mubi’s Fatherland expands to 45 screens. The Gothams (ceremony Nov. 30 in NYC) kicks off awards season.

Watch on Deadline

Watermelon Pictures Co-Founders Talk Future Plans & Growing Hollywood Support For Palestinian Stories: "We've Been Seeing A Renaissance With A Lot Of The A-Listers"

Awards Season Heats Up With 'The Only Living Pickpocket In New York,' 'Fatherland' & More - Specialty Preview

Wide release indies A24’s You Can See Everything , Black Bear’s Wicker and Laika’s Wildwood from Fathom Entertainment are still making a splash in theaters.

Everest: The Other Side , the latest epic documentary from NatGeo and Oscar-winning filmmakers Jimmy Chin and Chai Vasarhelyi ( Free Solo , Meru ), which just made the rounds at the fall festivals — Venice, Telluride and TIFF — follows elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson as they attempt a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Everest, the most difficult climb on the mountain. While thousands have summited via Nepal’s southeast ridge, only a handful have ever reached the top by this route, and no one had successfully skied down before. That doc has stunning visuals, and a story of passion, grief and determination. Chin and Vasarhelyi told Deadline recently it was the most difficult film they’ve ever made . At 551 locations, in theaters and Imax.

Breeder by Alex Goyette, an Independent Film Company and Shudder release, opened at 777 theaters Wednesday and is sticking there, heading into the weekend with about $275k. Daniel Doheny stars as Russell, a dedicated researcher who has spent years developing a solution to save the endangered bee population. Struggling with limited funding, his prospects brighten when an eccentric poodle breeder, Patti (Dot-Marie Jones), offers to sponsor his work. Drawn to her isolated ranch, Russell soon realizes that Patti’s ambitions extend far beyond saving bees. With Maddie Phillips and Paige McGarvin.

It world premiered at Tribeca Festival and sits at 86% on Rotten Tomatoes off 37 reviews.

Greenwich opens Queen At Sea at the Angelika Film Center in NYC. Lance Hammer’s ( Ballast ) first film in 20 years stars Juliette Binoche and Tom Courtenay.

Amanda (Binoche and her stepfather Martin (Courtnay) are struggling with a moral issue: Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall), suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control. Winner of Berlinale’s Silver Bear Jury Prize and the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance for Courtenay and Calder-Marshall. See Deadline review . At 93% with critics off 43 reviews. Starts a national expansion next week.

Who Killed Alex Odeh? from Watermelon Pictures, directed by Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, opens in NYC at the Quad Cinema, in Chicago at Uprising Theater and in LA at the Laemmle Glendale with a national expansion to follow. The true crime story about a political assassination won the U.S. Documentary Special Jury Award at Sundance.

In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. The doc reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long buried records come to light and the forces beyond a political assassination are finally confronted.

Briarcliff Entertainment is out with holiday horror-comedy Christmas At The Kringles on 1,825 screens. Directed by Kevin Lewis, written by Jack Imbrogno. The Severson family are starting fresh in a quiet suburban neighborhood with next-door neighbors, the Kringles, who celebrate Christmas year-round. What begins as charming quickly turns unsettling as Mark (Ron Livingston) and Julie (Rachel Bilson) grow concerned about their son’s growing attachment to the family, with good reason. Mark teams up with a badass Santa (Rob Riggle) in a high-stakes fight.

Roadside Attractions launches faith-based family musical Sight & Sound Presents: Joshua Live! on 1,230 screens. A production of Lancaster, Pa.-based Sight & Sound Theatres, the faith-based entertainment company that partners with distributors to bring its live stage productions to screen. Previous films include Noah — Live! (2025) and Daniel – Live! . This is story of Joshua, the successor of Moses, who led the Israelites to the promised land.

Heath ens by David Cowan and Shawn Hardin, debuting at the Laemmle Noho in Los Angeles, explores the situation of American adults who hide religious doubts or exaggerate how religious they are due to pressure they feel from those around them to conform. The doc follows five individuals over three years: a professional stuntwoman, two former preachers, the frontwoman of alt-pop band Transviolet, and a Christian musician, who first meet at a retreat in Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains. Each has quietly left the religion that raised them. Over a cathartic weekend, they resolve to reclaim their lives, taking back the slur “heathen” as a proud new identity. Then they return home to learn how much the truth will cost them. Self-distributed by producer Pale Blue Dot Films. Expands to San Francisco, New York and other markets next week.

Paging Hezbollah by Justin Folk launches on 250+ screens. Part history, part real-life espionage thriller, the documentary goes inside Israel’s September 2024 pager operation against Hezbollah, revealing how the devices were engineered, marketed and smuggled into Hezbollah’s communications network without detection. It traces the decades-long conflict between the two, from Mossad’s origins to the 2024 operation. Folk interviews Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Mossad Director David Barnea and General David Petraeus, alongside intelligence operatives, engineers and historians.

Produced and distributed by Aveiled Productions. The conservative filmmaker’s previous docs include 2024’s DEI takedown Am I Racist? (which grossed $12 million at the domestic box office) and What Is A Woman ? from 2022, both produced and released by right-wing media outlet The Daily Wire. Paging Hezbollah comes after inconclusive results in Israel’s national election, where neither Netanyahu’s hard-right coalition nor the opposition alliance received enough votes to govern.

article_text:
Issue

Art Fair Report: Regional Strengths

KIAF AND FRIEZE SEOUL

This year’s Seoul art week felt more crowded than ever. Running concurrently, Kiaf and Frieze Seoul shared the calendar with the Busan and Gwangju Biennales, giving collectors additional reasons to visit.

Kiaf returned for its 25th edition, its largest at 175 galleries, concluding its first five-year partnership with Frieze. The milestone arrives against a softening market: Korea’s art sales peaked near KRW 1 trillion (USD 743.8 million) in 2022 and have since fallen roughly 25 percent to around KRW 615 billion (USD 457.5 million).

At Kiaf, Dansaekhwa and postwar abstraction dominated. PYO offered Park Seo-Bo’s Ecriture No. 33-23 (2021) at roughly USD 190,000. Gallery Hyundai showed Lee Ufan’s Dialogue (2019), Kim Whanki’s Untitled (1970), and several 1990s Nam June Paik installations priced between USD 221,000 and 369,000. Its total sales reportedly exceeded KRW 1.2 billion (USD 892,600). Kukje Gallery anchored the upper end with Park Seo-Bo’s Ecriture No. 170606 (2022) and a rare Yoo Youngkuk oil canvas, Work (1979), which changed hands in the KRW 600–720 million (USD 450,000–540,000) range.

At the lower end were figurative, pop-derived works. Hakgojae presented Kim Jae Yong’s brightly colored Donut Fear sculptures (USD 50,000–80,000). Arario showed Lim Nosik’s hazy, violet-grey canvases, including Wildflower – Landscape 58 (2026), priced at roughly USD 8,760. Whitestone placed paintings by Aruta Soup, whose recurring, often bandaged rabbit motif draws on graffiti and club culture.

While Kiaf foregrounded domestic galleries, Frieze Seoul drew major Western dealers, including Gagosian, David Zwirner, and Hauser & Wirth. Kukje still claimed the week’s top result: a 1971 painting by Yoo Youngkuk sold in the KRW 2.2–2.5 billion range (roughly USD 1.6–1.8 million). The price was reported to be the highest ever paid at the fair for a work by a Korean artist since Frieze launched in Seoul in 2022. Other Kukje sales included Ha Chong-Hyun’s mixed-media work Post-Conjunction 21-512 (2021) for USD 253,000–303,600; an acrylic on ceramic by Park Seo-Bo, Ecriture No. 220611 (2022), for USD 250,000–300,000; and Suki Seokyeong Kang’s mixed-media work Mat #24-10 (2023–24) for USD 100,000–120,000.

White Cube sold Park Seo-Bo’s Ecriture No. 221121 (2022) for USD 300,000 and Ecriture No. 070909 (2007) for USD 190,000. Pace moved several pieces, among them Lee Ufan’s With Winds (1987). Lehmann Maupin dedicated its booth to Do Ho Suh’s thread drawings, coinciding with his survey at the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea, and sold three works by Kim Yun Shin, whose recent exhibition at the Hoam Museum of Art had raised her profile.

Frieze’s “Focus” section gathered smaller and mid-tier local galleries with experimental programs, including N/A, Pipe Gallery, and Foundry Seoul, which devoted its booth to Omyo Cho’s amorphous sculptures. The inaugural “Spotlight” section foregrounded overlooked 20th-century artists: Ames Yavuz showed Po Po’s conceptual pieces produced during Myanmar’s political isolation and censorship, while BAIK presented Han Youngsoo’s black-and-white photographs of postwar Seoul. Yoshiaki Inoue Gallery paired Etsuko Nakatsuji’s paintings with a suspended installation, positioning her as a forerunner of postwar Japanese installation art, while Tansbao Gallery and Art Exposure offered modernist canvases by Lain Singh Bangdel and Reba Hore, respectively.

The fairs pursue different ambitions: Kiaf consolidates Korea’s domestic ecosystem, while Frieze connects Korea to international dealers. Comparisons with Hong Kong persist: Art Basel’s Asian flagship draws a cross-border collector base Seoul has yet to match. But Seoul offers a different density, evident beyond the fair floor. “Neighborhood Nights” drew a broad public into galleries, museums, and after-hours events. In Hong Kong, satellite programming remains largely the preserve of professionals and VIPs. Seoul’s energy is more diffuse, connected to the cultural export engine carrying K-pop, K-drama, and K-fashion abroad.

TOKYO GENDAI

After Seoul, artgoers trickled into Japan for Tokyo Gendai, held September 11–13 at Pacifico Yokohama with 69 regional and overseas galleries. Its fourth edition comprised five sectors: the main Galleries section; Hana (“Flower”), dedicated to emerging or midcareer artists; Eda (“Branch”), highlighting historically significant names; Tane (“Seed”), featuring NFTs, film, VR, and other tech-driven projects; and the inaugural Miki (“Trunk”), focusing on paper-based and printed works.

Returning international galleries included Sadie Coles HQ, which showed British artist Sarah Lucas’s stuffed-nylon sculpture Blue Bunny (2025) and Japanese painter Yu Nishimura’s dreamlike portrait Diffraction (2026). Pace, whose Tokyo space survived its global downsizing, staged a solo presentation of American artist Lauren Quin’s vibrant tableaux, most of which sold within the first day.

Tokyo-based returnees included CON_, A Lighthouse called Kanata, Taka Ishii Gallery, TARO NASU, and KOTARO NUKAGA. The latter sold more than 20 works, including two of Keita Morimoto’s neon-drenched canvases capturing Tokyo’s urban alienation, each priced between USD 40,000 and 60,000. CON_ devoted its booth to Yukino Yamanaka’s figurative paintings, selling more than five for under USD 10,000 each. Predominantly modest prices and a focus on younger artists gave new buyers a lower-risk entry point.

Japan defied the global downturn in 2024 with a two-percent increase in art sales, retaining its position as the second-largest market in Asia. Growth slowed by one percent in 2025, likely reflecting rising fuel and freight costs and a chronically weak yen. Nevertheless, a robust institutional infrastructure, younger high-net-worth domestic collectors, and foreign dealers’ sustained engagement have helped the market hold steady.

Tokyo Gendai has adapted accordingly. Last year, it moved to autumn to align with the Korean fairs and attract more American and European visitors deterred by Japan’s summer heat. Next year, it relocates to Ariake GYM-EX, a former 2020 Olympic arena, with new dates—November 4–7, 2027. The more central venue and overlap with Art Week Tokyo signal an effort to cultivate an internally coordinated program.

ART JAKARTA

Art Jakarta’s 16th edition, held October 2–4 at JIExpo Kemayoran, drew a record 41,646 visitors, up from approximately 38,000 last year. The roster held steady at 75 exhibitors, while international participation dipped from 35 galleries to 33—the first decline since the fair resumed after the pandemic in 2022.

Indonesian galleries were prominent in “Spot,” the sector for oversized installations, where themes of kinship and land contributed to a political register beyond the spectacle of scale. ROH paired Albertho Wanma’s The Nature Womb (Karwar Series) (2024), which draws on the ancestral statues of Papua’s Biak people, with Budi Santoso’s Mother Trees (2026)—totemic forms whose stacked heads and raised fists suggest solidarity. SAL Project mounted Angki Purbandono’s Berbunga-bunga: Tribute to Red Cross Movement in South Papua (2026), a towering bamboo cross honoring communities who erect wooden crosses to protest plantations and food estates. ara contemporary presented Nguyễn Phương Linh’s Pulse 1 and Pulse 2 (both 2026), PVC sheets printed with digital images that evoke flesh and landscape, related to her presentation in the Uzbekistan Pavilion at the Venice Biennale.

Accessible prices offered multiple entry points for collectors. ara brought 21 artists, with prices ranging from USD 300 for S. Urubingwaru’s small oils to USD 17,000 for Nazif Lopulissa’s nearly three-meter Drinking Seawater (2023). Sullivan+Strumpf offered a selection of Wisnu Auri’s mixed-media vignettes at USD 1,100–1420 alongside Dawn Ng’s Tender Eruptions (2026), priced at USD 58,000. Intergenerational breadth was present at Gajah Gallery, whose 18-artist booth included Mangu Putra’s hyperrealist Stage (2025) alongside his son Jemana Murti’s 3D-printed reworkings of Balinese motifs. Among the 19 first-time exhibitors were Seoul’s BHAK, Kyoto’s YUMEKOUBOU, Tokyo’s Misako & Rosen, and Hong Kong’s PHD Group. Their arrival replenished a roster that lost Kaikai Kiki Gallery, Tina Keng Gallery, and Manila’s The Drawing Room.

Government-funded sections broadened participation: “Korea Focus,” supported by South Korea’s culture ministry, expanded from 12 to 14 young galleries, while the new “AJ Scope,” backed by Indonesia’s Ministry of Culture, brought six independent art market initiatives from across the country to Jakarta. These efforts positioned the fair as a collaborative platform seeking to deepen engagement both at home and abroad.

"她讲述的许多故事，都是巴西近代史关键事件的切片。阿尔塔米拉（Altamira）的会面、500周年庆典期间与原住民的游行、塞多广场（praça da Sé）上聚集的形形色色抗议活动、对奇科·门德斯（Chico Enfoco（当时一所重要的摄影学校）学习和工作后，深夜才回家。因此，当时社会运动正在为之奋斗争取公民自由的抗争，与她亲身经历的个人自由追求产生了共鸣。她所拍摄的少数群体（特别是当时女性群体）对自由与认可的追求，同样也是她自己的个人追求。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "在一次谈论罗莎于1980年代初期创作的、从“巨大而亲密”二分法视角观察圣保罗的系列作品时，我们开始观看如今已广为人知的街头儿童在塞多广场喷泉嬉戏的照片。我有些不经意地评论道，比起她为同一个项目拍摄的中产阶级儿童——那些住在窗户装有铁栏杆的公寓里、在混凝土车库等狭窄空间玩耍的孩子们——街头儿童看起来要快乐和自由得多。她神情严肃地看着我的眼睛说道：“对，但塞多广场的男孩们随后会挤在一起睡在地铁通风口上，好不挨冻……”她随后又轻声自言自语道：“这是一场悲剧。”这段对话一直留在我脑海中。几天后，当我们看到瓜拉尼-卡约瓦人（Guarani-Kaiová）的照片时——这是当前遭受暴力最严重的族群之一，她曾近距离见证了他们的灭绝（因为只有呆在家里的才是病人）——她告诉我，她担心展览会显得太沉重、太悲伤。看着这些照片，对我而言，没有什么比这更遥远了。", "我花了一会儿才将这两者联系起来。但我随即明白，我当时面对的是两个档案库，它们看似相似却并不相同。我正沉浸在影像档案中，它充满历史重要性，记录精确。它是摄影师与被拍摄者之间信任、互动和对话的见证。它无一例外地展现了被拍摄者的尊严。然而，我也正沉浸在第二个档案库中，即照片瞬间之外环绕着的故事。之前发生了什么，之后又发生了什么。每一个肖像背后每个人的生活、现实和抗争。这个档案库储存在罗莎的记忆中，而她当时正慷慨地与我分享。这两个档案库之间的交织，正是她对展览的看法与我的看法产生差异的原因。我看到的是面带微笑的街头男孩，他们把城市的街道当成欢乐游戏的领地，在她的镜头前摆出超级英雄的姿态。而她看到的是他们在寒冷中没有过夜的地方、饱受冻馁。我看到的是瓜拉尼-卡约瓦人直视镜头，昂首挺胸地面对周遭的贫困，并用他们手头仅有的东西维系传统。而她看到的是（用她的话说）“无声的灭绝”以及马托格罗索州地主的暴力。我于是明白，我那里的部分工作也是将这两个档案库连接起来。", Isso se repetiria nas outras inúmeras conversas que eu e ela teríamos ao longo do tempo: Rosa sempre foi uma interlocutora generosa, sempre falou com franqueza, dizendo tudo o que tinha pra dizer, e sempre compartilhou créditos e buscou agregar pessoas, com um verdadeiro senso de comunidade em torno da fotografia documental brasileira. Eduardo e eu saímos daquela primeira entrevista com muitas ideias de como dar continuidade ao nosso projeto, que girava em torno da participação brasileira nos Colóquios Latino-Americanos de Fotografia dos anos 70 e 80. Ela nos deu muito material histórico para trabalhar, e vários outros nomes para novas entrevistas."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rosa e eu continuamos em contato, construindo uma colaboração profissional baseada no entusiasmo pelo poder da fotografia de apoiar as lutas democráticas de ontem e de hoje. Rosa também me incluiu em projetos e eventos que participou, como o lançamento do livro Máquinas Paradas, Fotógrafos em Ação , em 2017 . O livro traz uma documentação importante sobre as greves do ABC, que estavam a ponto de comemorar 40 anos, com imagens de dez fotojornalistas do período, incluindo Rosa, e organização de Ennio Brauns e Adilson Ruiz. Essa proximidade me deixou cada vez mais interessada no trabalho dela enquanto fotógrafa mulher, parte de uma geração de mulheres que foi pioneira no fotojornalismo contemporâneo brasileiro. A profissão como um todo estava se transformando naquela época, e essa geração foi fundamental para o estabelecimento do fotojornalismo de autor que se formou a partir da tímida e gradual distensão da ditadura, e do aparecimento da imprensa alternativa, crítica da ditadura, em meados da década de 1970. O meu interesse sobre o aspecto militante contra a ditadura da obra da Rosa, visto por meio da cobertura das greves do ABC, resultou em um artigo para a ZUM em 2018.", "links": [{"text": "artigo para a ZUM", "url": "https://revistazum.com.br/radar/rosa-gauditano-greves-abc/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Não eram apenas as greves que estavam de aniversário por aquele período. No ano em que nos conhecemos, Rosa estava completando 40 anos de carreira. Eu imagino, mas nunca falamos diretamente sobre isso, que por este motivo ela estava também revisando o seu próprio arquivo. Ela sempre teve plena consciência da importância de manter um arquivo, e como eu pude vir a testemunhar mais tarde – nove anos depois eu conheceria em detalhes esse arquivo – ela teve o cuidado de guardar e manter tudo o que produziu. Já na primeira visita, para a entrevista de 2016, ela tinha mostrado o quarto em que mantinha dezenas de gavetas com as fotos que realizou durante toda a carreira e com as publicações onde elas aparecem. Naquele momento conversamos sobre como era complicado, e custoso, manter esse espaço climatizado 24 horas por dia. Manter os próprios arquivos, e o que fazer com eles para assegurar a preservação física e disponibilizar em alguma medida acesso público, é uma questão antiga, mas ainda muito relevante para muitos fotógrafos brasileiros, como era para Rosa."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Não muito tempo depois do meu primeiro encontro com a Rosa, ela foi morar em Londres. Neste período, a nossa colaboração de trabalho levou à descoberta de afinidades pessoais, e a proximidade em Londres possibilitou que continuássemos amigas para além da fotografia. Num dia muito frio em um janeiro já distante, ela me convidou pra ir ouvir o companheiro dela, o Ife Tolentino, tocar chorinho no norte de Londres, e eu resolvi inventar uma desculpa pra não ir porque estava com preguiça. Ela me repreendeu, citando uma frase do pai dela: só fica em casa quem está doente."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Pensando nisso hoje, para mim essa frase – e o nosso diálogo ali – representa tão bem a Rosa, tanto a pessoa, a amiga, quanto a fotógrafa. Ir até o outro, estabelecer diálogo, contato, troca, são atributos fundamentais para o fotografo documental, e aparecem claramente no trabalho da Rosa. Feito sempre de perto, quase nunca usando teleobjetiva, os retratos das prostitutas de São Paulo, das mais de 50 etnias indígenas que ela visitou, das frequentadoras de boates lésbicas, ou dos participantes das mais diversas festas populares pelo país, mostram uma cumplicidade com a câmera que só pode ser fruto de troca, não de tomada. Da mesma forma, a citação do pai de Rosa também me lembrou uma frase que ouvi de outra gigante da profissão, Nair Benedicto, quando eu a entrevistei também há 10 anos, poucas semanas depois da Rosa (e que também virou artigo pra ZUM ). Em um certo momento da nossa conversa, a Nair falou que, pra ela, a particularidade do fotógrafo, ou a diferença entre o fotógrafo e outra profissão, é que o fotógrafo ‘vai até lá’. Ela ou ele vai nos lugares e vê. Testemunha. Compartilha. Toma conhecimento. E a partir daí pode também, se quiser, agir. Décadas depois, com o ritmo de trabalho mais calmo, e com a vantagem do olhar retrospectivo, é mais fácil rever, reorganizar, e ressignificar o próprio trabalho. As fotografias e séries guardadas por tanto tempo podem então contar novas histórias. Um ano atrás, em agosto de 2025, mais precisamente no dia 7, a fotógrafa Rosa Gauditano nos deixou. Ela tinha 70 anos.

Eu conheci a Rosa há exatos 10 anos, em 2016. Eu e o Eduardo Costa fomos até a casa em que ela morava, na zona oeste de São Paulo, para fazer uma entrevista. Naquela época nós estávamos começando um projeto que, uma década depois, me traria para uma bolsa de sete meses em Munique, de onde escrevo esse texto. Eu e o Eduardo chegamos na casa dela naquele dia, nos sentamos na mesa da sala, e a ouvimos por mais de três horas. Isso se repetiria nas outras inúmeras conversas que eu e ela teríamos ao longo do tempo: Rosa sempre foi uma interlocutora generosa, sempre falou com franqueza, dizendo tudo o que tinha pra dizer, e sempre compartilhou créditos e buscou agregar pessoas, com um verdadeiro senso de comunidade em torno da fotografia documental brasileira. Eduardo e eu saímos daquela primeira entrevista com muitas ideias de como dar continuidade ao nosso projeto, que girava em torno da participação brasileira nos Colóquios Latino-Americanos de Fotografia dos anos 70 e 80. Ela nos deu muito material histórico para trabalhar, e vários outros nomes para novas entrevistas.

Rosa e eu continuamos em contato, construindo uma colaboração profissional baseada no entusiasmo pelo poder da fotografia de apoiar as lutas democráticas de ontem e de hoje. De forma espontânea, por vezes nossos caminhos foram se cruzando. Rosa também me incluiu em projetos e eventos que participou, como o lançamento do livro Máquinas Paradas, Fotógrafos em Ação , em 2017 . O livro traz uma documentação importante sobre as greves do ABC, que estavam a ponto de comemorar 40 anos, com imagens de dez fotojornalistas do período, incluindo Rosa, e organização de Ennio Brauns e Adilson Ruiz. Essa proximidade me deixou cada vez mais interessada no trabalho dela enquanto fotógrafa mulher, parte de uma geração de mulheres que foi pioneira no fotojornalismo contemporâneo brasileiro. A profissão como um todo estava se transformando naquela época, e essa geração foi fundamental para o estabelecimento do fotojornalismo de autor que se formou a partir da tímida e gradual distensão da ditadura, e do aparecimento da imprensa alternativa, crítica da ditadura, em meados da década de 1970. O meu interesse sobre o aspecto militante contra a ditadura da obra da Rosa, visto por meio da cobertura das greves do ABC, resultou em um artigo para a ZUM em 2018.

Não eram apenas as greves que estavam de aniversário por aquele período. No ano em que nos conhecemos, Rosa estava completando 40 anos de carreira. Eu imagino, mas nunca falamos diretamente sobre isso, que por este motivo ela estava também revisando o seu próprio arquivo. Ela sempre teve plena consciência da importância de manter um arquivo, e como eu pude vir a testemunhar mais tarde – nove anos depois eu conheceria em detalhes esse arquivo – ela teve o cuidado de guardar e manter tudo o que produziu. Já na primeira visita, para a entrevista de 2016, ela tinha mostrado o quarto em que mantinha dezenas de gavetas com as fotos que realizou durante toda a carreira e com as publicações onde elas aparecem. Naquele momento conversamos sobre como era complicado, e custoso, manter esse espaço climatizado 24 horas por dia. Esta preocupação pessoal levaria a Rosa a participar, já em 2024, da organização do seminário ‘Fototeca Brasileira: políticas para preservação da memória fotográfica’ no CPF-SESC que trouxe fotógrafos e pesquisadores para debaterem juntos a possibilidade de construção de uma política nacional para a fotografia, incluindo a sua preservação. Manter os próprios arquivos, e o que fazer com eles para assegurar a preservação física e disponibilizar em alguma medida acesso público, é uma questão antiga, mas ainda muito relevante para muitos fotógrafos brasileiros, como era para Rosa.

Não muito tempo depois do meu primeiro encontro com a Rosa, ela foi morar em Londres. E em seguida eu fui também. Por coincidência, nós duas atravessamos o Atlântico por questões do coração. Neste período, a nossa colaboração de trabalho levou à descoberta de afinidades pessoais, e a proximidade em Londres possibilitou que continuássemos amigas para além da fotografia. Num dia muito frio em um janeiro já distante, ela me convidou pra ir ouvir o companheiro dela, o Ife Tolentino, tocar chorinho no norte de Londres, e eu resolvi inventar uma desculpa pra não ir porque estava com preguiça. Ela me repreendeu, citando uma frase do pai dela: só fica em casa quem está doente.

Pensando nisso hoje, para mim essa frase – e o nosso diálogo ali – representa tão bem a Rosa, tanto a pessoa, a amiga, quanto a fotógrafa. Porque como pessoa ela estava em constante movimento, sempre expansiva e gregária. Características que também é justo considerar que são um bom ponto de partida para a profissão de fotógrafa. Ir até o outro, estabelecer diálogo, contato, troca, são atributos fundamentais para o fotografo documental, e aparecem claramente no trabalho da Rosa. Feito sempre de perto, quase nunca usando teleobjetiva, os retratos das prostitutas de São Paulo, das mais de 50 etnias indígenas que ela visitou, das frequentadoras de boates lésbicas, ou dos participantes das mais diversas festas populares pelo país, mostram uma cumplicidade com a câmera que só pode ser fruto de troca, não de tomada. Da mesma forma, a citação do pai de Rosa também me lembrou uma frase que ouvi de outra gigante da profissão, Nair Benedicto, quando eu a entrevistei também há 10 anos, poucas semanas depois da Rosa (e que também virou artigo pra ZUM ). Em um certo momento da nossa conversa, a Nair falou que, pra ela, a particularidade do fotógrafo, ou a diferença entre o fotógrafo e outra profissão, é que o fotógrafo ‘vai até lá’. Ela ou ele vai nos lugares e vê. Testemunha. Compartilha. Toma conhecimento. E a partir daí pode também, se quiser, agir. Não fica em casa, porque só fica em casa quem está doente.

O processo de revisitar o próprio arquivo também não é algo tão raro entre fotógrafos. Os anos de maior produção – geralmente os anos iniciais da carreira – são mais dinâmicos e propiciam um acúmulo de projetos por vezes em detrimento de um olhar mais demorado e reflexivo. Décadas depois, com o ritmo de trabalho mais calmo, e com a vantagem do olhar retrospectivo, é mais fácil rever, reorganizar, e ressignificar o próprio trabalho. As fotografias e séries guardadas por tanto tempo podem então contar novas histórias. Um dos maiores exemplos que vêm à mente é o de Claudia Andujar, que fez o processo de ressignificar em arte uma produção anterior, que tinha na origem objetivos jornalísticos ou de documentação para fins puramente práticos. No caso de Rosa, esse processo, iniciado em fins da década de 2010, ajudou a redescobrir séries mais antigas, que permaneceram inéditas ou pouco divulgadas, e que têm enorme importância histórica pois contam de diversos ângulos o longo caminho de redemocratização do pais. Ele também desembocou em dois livros que ela mesma editou.

O primeiro, Elas por Elas , foi um protótipo que combinou dois ensaios do final da década de 1970. Em 1976 Rosa realizou junto com o amigo, também fotógrafo, Ayrton de Magalhães, uma série em um prostíbulo do centro de São Paulo. Foi a primeira de sua carreira, quando ainda era estudante, indo escondida do pai e revelando e ampliando as fotos em casa. Na época, as fotos foram publicadas na revista Photoptica e no jornal Versus , mas não circularam de forma muito mais ampla no Brasil. No exterior é outro assunto: Rosa mandou essa série para o Primeiro Colóquio Latino-Americano de Fotografia, realizado na Cidade do México em 1978, e ela foi selecionada para a exposição coletiva Hecho en Latinoamerica , que acompanhou o evento, e para o catálogo. Além disso, a exposição viajou por dezenas de países na Europa e América Latina. Foi pesquisando esse evento, e portanto por meio desse ensaio, que eu cheguei até a Rosa. Minha pesquisa revelou que as fotos dela receberam destaque particular em diversas revistas europeias. O segundo ensaio que ela retirou das gavetas para publicar em Elas por Elas veio dos arquivos da Veja . Em 1979 a revista a chamou para fazer uma reportagem sobre a vida e a sociabilidade das lésbicas em São Paulo. Segundo ela, outros fotógrafos – todos homens – tinham sido chamados mas não conseguiram fazer a pauta. Rosa conseguiu, mas a Veja nunca publicou, por considerarem o tema controverso ainda sob a ditadura, e o ensaio permaneceu por décadas inédito. O livro Elas por Elas também permaneceu apenas como protótipo, mas o ensaio das lésbicas finalmente ganhou destaque na Bienal de 2023.

Com o segundo livro eu estive mais envolvida. A Mesma Luta foi publicado em 2021, a partir de uma seleção da ampla documentação que Rosa fez dos movimentos sociais entre 1976 e 1985, focando mais uma vez nas atuação das mulheres. Esse mergulho no arquivo, desenvolvido principalmente no tempo em que ela trabalhou para o jornal Versus , trouxe das gavetas fotos do Movimento do Custo de Vida, encabeçado por mulheres da periferia de São Paulo, dos Encontros da Mulher Paulista, do Movimento Negro, das greves do ABC, entre muitas outras. É um trabalho de fotojornalismo, desenvolvido na maior parte como freelance , que mostra uma clara autoria: uma liberdade tanto estética (como fotografar) quanto temática (o que fotografar). Rosa compartilhou comigo conjuntos de fotos em estágios prévios do processo de seleção, e depois me convidou para escrever um dos textos do livro. A Mesma Luta ganhou prêmios nacionais e internacionais, inclusive o destaque da Convocatória de Fotolivros da Revista ZUM em 2021.

Mais ou menos nessa época a Rosa tinha voltado pro Brasil. Ela tinha se cansado do frio da Inglaterra e da distancia da família – principalmente dos netos. Nós continuamos a amizade por meio de longas conversas no WhatsApp. A gente conversava sobre tudo, como sempre, mas alguns assuntos eram pauta toda vez: a situação política do Brasil, a preservação do arquivo dela e, mais recentemente, o legado do trabalho dela, que estava também sendo reconhecido por instituições nos EUA. Durante uma dessas conversas, ela me contou que faria uma exposição comemorando os 50 anos de carreira no Museu da Cidade de São Paulo. Ela pediu meu currículo. E de repente eu era parte integrante de uma nova etapa da revisão do arquivo da Rosa. Eu me lembro de ter pensado, que sortuda que eu sou, poder trabalhar com o que eu gosto e com quem eu gosto.

Um ano atrás, em julho de 2025, eu passei um mês no Brasil trabalhando na exposição junto com a Rosa. Dentro desse mês, por uma semana eu fiquei na casa dela, convivendo e olhando de perto o seu arquivo. Ela ia abrindo gavetas, portfólios e HDs e tirando cromos, negativos, tiragens novas e vintage, e fotos escaneadas e já feitas em digital. Nós passamos os dias fazendo isso, mas também tomando café, caminhando no mato, fazendo crochê e vendo filme de noite, cozinhando e comendo juntas. Mas, acima de tudo, eu passei esse tempo ouvindo. Eu me tornei um grande ouvido – eu ouvi, gravei, anotei tantas histórias quanto ela tinha pra contar. E ela queria falar, e não faltavam assuntos. Cada foto, cada livro, cada sentada na mesa de jantar pra tomar um café quentinho, abria uma nova gaveta de lembranças da juventude, memórias profissionais, planos e possibilidades de futuros projetos.

Muitas das histórias que ela contou são recortes de acontecimentos-chave da história recente do Brasil. O encontro de Altamira, a marcha com os indígenas durante as celebrações dos 500 anos, a praça da Sé tomada por tantos e diferentes protestos, a visita à família de Chico Mendes. Por vezes, essas histórias se misturavam também com as histórias pessoais da vida dela. Em especial histórias sobre a violência da ditadura – tão visível nas fotos da polícia reprimindo manifestação na praça da Sé ou usando o ‘brucutu’ para ir pra cima dos participantes de uma marcha de Primeiro de Maio – se misturavam na mesa do café com histórias sobre a violência na maioria das vezes simbólica que Rosa vivenciava na mesma época em casa. Vinham então as histórias da juventude, quando o pai tradicionalista não aceitava que ela saísse de casa quando ela queria, e que tivesse namorados. Contrastando com a mãe independente, que trabalhava fora e comprou para ela a primeira câmera, o pai também não aceitava que ela se tornasse fotógrafa. Então a luta pelas liberdades civis que os movimentos sociais estavam travando naquele momento ressonava com a busca de liberdade pessoal que ela viveu na própria pele. A busca de liberdade e reconhecimento das minorias que ela fotografou, em especial a das mulheres naquele momento, era a busca pessoal dela também.

Durante uma conversa sobre a série que Rosa fez no início da década de 1980 sobre São Paulo vista a partir da dicotomia entre ‘gigante e intimista’, começamos a ver fotos, hoje bastante conhecidas, de crianças de rua brincando na fonte da praça da Sé. Eu comentei, meio sem pensar, que elas pareciam muito mais alegres e livres do que as crianças de classe média que ela fotografou para o mesmo projeto, moradoras de apartamentos com grades nas janelas e brincando em espaços apertados, como garagens de concreto. Ela ficou séria, me olhou nos olhos, e disse: é, mas os meninos da Sé iam depois dormir juntinhos em cima da ventilação do metrô, pra não passarem frio… E ela completou baixinho, pra ela mesma: uma tragédia . Olhando as fotos, para mim nada parecia mais longe disso.

Eu demorei um momento pra ligar as duas coisas. Mas daí entendi que eu estava ali diante de dois arquivos, que eram parecidos mas não o mesmo. Eu estava mergulhando no arquivo de imagens, cheio de importância histórica, de registros precisos. Testemunha da confiança, interação e do diálogo entre fotógrafa e fotografado. Que invariavelmente mostra a dignidade do fotografado. Mas eu estava também mergulhando em um segundo arquivo, o das histórias daquilo que circundava o instante da foto. O que veio antes e o que veio depois. A vida, a realidade, a luta de cada pessoa por trás de cada retrato. Esse arquivo estava localizado na memória da Rosa e ela estava generosamente compartilhando comigo naquele momento. E a interação entre os dois arquivos era o que causava a discrepância entre a visão dela sobre a exposição e a minha. Eu via os meninos de rua sorridentes, reclamando as ruas da cidade pra brincadeira alegre e posando como super-heróis pra câmera dela. Ela os via passando frio sem ter onde dormir à noite. Ela via o ‘genocídio silencioso’ (nas palavras dela) e a violência dos donos de terras mato-grossenses. Eu então entendi que parte do meu trabalho ali era também conectar esses dois arquivos.

Depois dessa semana juntas nós ainda tivemos uma reunião. No dia seguinte, eu peguei o avião de volta pra Londres. Um pouco mais tarde, nesse mesmo dia, Rosa faleceu repentinamente.

No meio da dor da perda, é também doloroso pensar que um desses arquivos se foi. Me dá um grande senso de responsabilidade com o que me foi compartilhado ali na mesa do café. Felizmente, o arquivo de fotos, tão bem organizado por ela em vida, junto com as publicações, clippings , tiragens e efemérides, permanece e agora está sendo cuidado, no sentido físico e também emocional, pela filha dela, a Camila. É comum dizer que uma pessoa cheia de vida não desaparece completamente. Os arquivos da Rosa, embora não mais completos, com certeza vão poder manter o olhar dela vivo por muito mais tempo – e, se depender de nós, contando mais histórias. ///

Erika Zerwes é doutora em História pela UNICAMP. Especializada em história da fotografia, é autora do livro Tempo de Guerra. Cultura visual e cultura política nas fotografias dos fundadores da agência Magnum e co-autora de Mulheres Fotógrafas/Mulheres Fotografadas. Fotografia e gênero na América Latina e Cultura Visual, Imagens na Modernidade , finalista do prêmio Jabuti. Atualmente é fellow no Käte Hamburger Kolleg global dis:connect, da LMU Munique.
article_translation_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/1978_1-GREVE-FORD-2.png?resize=1024%2C678&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "罗莎·加迪塔诺(Rosa Gauditano)在1978年福特工厂的罢工中遭到拍卖。", "credit": "ZUM · Instituto Moreira Salles", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一年前,八月 2025 更确切地说,当天 7 摄影师罗莎·加迪塔诺(Rosa Gauditano)离开了我们。 70 多年。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我认识了罗莎10年前,2016年,我和爱德华·科斯塔去了她住的房子,在西部圣保罗地区,进行面试。当时我们正在开始一个项目,十年后,我会带我到一个七个月的慕尼黑交易所,从那里我写这篇文章。我和爱德华在那天到达她的房子,我们坐在房间的桌子上,并听到她超过三个小时。我們會隨著時間的推移:羅莎一直是一個慷慨的對話者,總是說誠實,說出他所說的一切,總是分享信件,並尋求加入人們,一個真正的社區感,周圍的巴西紀錄片攝影。 埃達多和我從那個第一次面試,有許多想法如何繼續我們的項目,它旋轉了巴西參與的拉丁美洲攝影集團的70年代和80年代。面试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗莎和我继续保持联系,建立一个基于热情的专业合作,以摄影的力量支持昨天和今天的民主斗争。自发,有时我们的道路已经交叉。 罗莎也包括我在参与的项目和活动,如出版的书停机,摄影师在行动 ,在2017年。 这本书带来了一个重要的文档关于ABC罢工,即即将庆祝40年,与十个摄影记者的图像包括Rosa,以及Ennio Brauns和Adilson Ruiz的组织。这种接近让我越来越感兴趣她的工作作为女摄影师,是巴西当代摄影新闻领域的先驱的一代妇女的一部分。 作为一个整体的职业在那个时代正在转变,而这一代人是创作者摄影新闻的建立至关重要的,从独裁的可耻和逐步分离形成,以及替代媒体的出现,对独裁的批评,在1970年代中期,我对反对罗莎作品的独裁政权的激进观点的兴趣,通过ABC罢工的覆盖,结果是2018年ZUM的文章。", "links": [{"text": "artigo para a ZUM", "url": "https://revistazum.com.br/radar/rosa-gauditano-greves-abc/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那时,我们不只是一个生日罢工,那时我们认识的年份,罗莎已经完成了。 40 我想象,但我们从来没有直接谈论它,这就是为什么她也在审查自己的文件。 她总是充分意识到保持一个文件的重要性,以及我如何后来可以见证 - 九年后我会详细了解这个文件 - 她注意到保存和保持所有它产生的。 2016 她她展示了房间,在那里她保留了数十张照片,她在整个职业生涯中拍摄的照片和出版物,他们出现在那里。 那时,我们谈论了如何复杂,昂贵,保持这个空调空间24小时。 这个个人担忧会导致Rosa参加,已经在2024年,在CPF-SESC的“Brazilian PhotoTeca: 摄影记忆保护政策”研讨会的组织,带来摄影师和研究人员一起讨论的可能性。保持自己的档案,以及如何与他们进行,以确保物理保存,并在某种程度上提供公众访问,这是一个古老的问题,但仍然非常相关的许多巴西摄影师,如罗莎。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与玫瑰的第一次约会后不久,她去了伦敦,然后我也去了,偶然,我们两人通过大西洋的心脏问题,在这个时期,我们的合作导致了个人亲密关系的发现,伦敦的亲密关系使我们能够继续朋友,除了照片。我决定发明一个借口,不去,因为她很生气,她对我抱怨,引用她父亲的一句话:只有病人留在家里。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "想想这一点今天,对我来说,这个句子 - 和我们的对话在那里 - 代表玫瑰,无论是人,朋友,还是摄影师. 因为作为一个人,她一直在不断的运动,总是扩展和格雷格里亚. 特点,也是公平的考虑,这是一个很好的出发点为摄影师的职业。 去另一个,建立对话,联系,交换,是纪录片摄影师的基本属性,并在玫瑰的工作中显而易见。首頁 〉外文書 〉文學 〉西洋文學 〉The Portraits of the Prostitutes of São Paulo 50 她访问的原住民民族,来自女同性恋游艇的参观者,或者来自全国最多流行的派对的参与者,展示了相机的复杂性,这只能是交换的结果,而不是拍摄的结果。 同样,罗莎的父亲的引用也提醒我一个句子,我听到另一个巨头的职业,奈尔贝尼迪克托,当我采访她也有 10 几年,几周在我们对话的一段时间里,纳伊尔说,对她来说,摄影师的特点,或者摄影师和其他职业之间的区别,是摄影师“走到那里”。她或他去的地方,看到。 见证人. 分享. 了解。 从那时起,你也可以,如果你愿意,采取行动. 不留在家里,因为只有在家里的人生病。", "links": [{"text": "artigo pra ZUM", "url": "https://revistazum.com.br/entrevistas/conversa-nair-benedicto/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/7693_1_071_20.png?resize=1024%2C683&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "Rosa Gauditano - 通常是职业生涯的早期年份 - 更动态,有时会导致项目积累,而不是更长时间的和更有反思的观点。 几十年后,随着工作节奏更平静,并且有回顾的观点的好处,更容易重新审视,重新组织,并重新描述工作本身。新的故事. 最伟大的例子是克劳迪亚·安杜贾尔,谁做了在艺术中重定义一个以前的制作的过程,谁起源的报纸或文档的目的,纯粹实用的目的. 在罗莎的情况下,这个过程,开始于2010年代末,有助于重新发现更古老的系列,这些仍然是未出版或不公开,并且具有巨大的历史意义,因为它们从不同的角度讲述了祖国重新民主化的漫长道路。她自己写的两本书。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第一個,Elas為Elas ,是一個原型,結合了兩個實驗的終於1970年代。在1976年,Rosa與他的朋友,也攝影師,Ayrton Magellanes,在聖保羅的中心的<unk>子上進行了一系列。 它是他的第一個職業,當他還是一個學生,從父親隱藏,並揭露和擴大照片在家裡。在国外是另一个主题:Rosa发送了这个系列到第一张拉丁美洲摄影集,在1978年在墨西哥城举行,她被选为集体展览Hecho en Latinoamerica ,伴随了活动,并为目录。 此外,展览旅行了数十个国家在欧洲和拉丁美洲。 她正在调查这个事件,因此通过这个实验,我到达Rosa。她在各个欧洲杂志中特别突出。 她从纸箱中提取的第二次试验,以便在《她们》上发表,来自《看》的档案。 在1979年,该杂志呼吁她对圣保罗的女同性恋生活和社交性进行报告. 她说,其他摄影师 - 所有男人 - 都被召唤,但无法做假设。她们的书也只是一个原型,但女同性恋的试验最终在2023年比亚尔中获得了突出点。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与第二本书我更感兴趣. 同一斗争出版于2021年,从罗莎从1976年至1985年间的社会运动中所做的广泛文档的选择,再次专注于妇女的行为。 该档案的潜水,主要是在她为《Versus》工作时开发的,从纸箱中带来了由圣保罗郊区的妇女主导的生活成本运动,保罗妇女的聚会,黑色运动,罢工的照片。ABC,包括许多其他. 这是一个摄影新闻工作,主要是作为自由人开发的,它显示了一个明确的作者:一个美学自由(如拍摄)和主题自由(什么拍摄)。 罗莎与我分享了照片集在选举过程的早期阶段,然后邀请我写一本书的文本。 同样的斗争赢得了国家和国际奖项,包括2021年ZUM杂志的摄影奖提名的突出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/elas-por-elas-1024x1020.png?resize=1024%2C1020&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "《她们为她们》 罗莎·加迪塔诺(Rosa Gauditano)2017年", "credit": "ZUM · Instituto Moreira Salles", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/a-mesma-luta.png?resize=617%2C820&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "《同一斗争》Rosa Gauditano,2021年", "credit": "ZUM · Instituto Moreira Salles", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在那段时间里,罗莎已经回到巴西,她已经厌倦了英格兰的寒冷和家庭的距离 - 主要是孙子,我们通过WhatsApp的长时间聊天继续了友谊,我们谈论了一切,像往常一样,但一些事情都是常见的:巴西的政治状况,保留她的档案,最近,她的工作遗产,这也是美国机构认可的。庆祝圣保罗城博物馆50年的职业生涯,她要求我的课程,突然我是罗莎档案审查的新阶段的一部分,我记得我以为,我有多幸运,我能与我喜欢和我喜欢的人一起工作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一年前,在2025年7月,我在巴西度过了一个月,在展览会上与罗莎一起工作,在这个月内,一周我住在她的家里,生活在一起,仔细观察她的档案,她打开了纸箱,钱包和HD,并拍摄了克罗姆,负,新和古老的拍摄,并在数字上扫描和拍摄的照片。我们花了几天做这件事,但也喝咖啡,在草坪上散步,做草坪和观看夜间电影,吃饭和一起吃饭,但是,最重要的是,我花了这个时间听,我成为一个大耳朵,我听,写,记得她想讲的这么多故事,她想说话,没有问题,每张照片,每本书,每张坐在晚餐桌上喝一杯热咖啡,打开了一个新的青春回忆,职业记忆,计划和未来项目的可能性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i0.wp.com/revistazum.com.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_1996.png?resize=1024%2C768&ssl=1", "alt": "", "caption": "伊卡罗杂志与罗莎·加迪塔诺的封面,在摄影师的档案中. 照片 Erika Zerwes,2025。", "credit": "ZUM · Instituto Moreira Salles", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她所讲的许多故事是巴西最近历史的关键事件的缩写,阿尔塔米拉的会面,与500周年庆祝活动的原住民的游行,由许多不同的抗议所带来的塞广场,访问奇科门德斯的家人,有时这些故事也与她生命的个人故事相结合。“brucutu”去上参加一个5月1日游行的参与者 – 他们在咖啡桌上与关于暴力的故事混合,大多数象征性时刻罗莎在同一时期在家里经历。 然后,青春的故事,当传统主义的父亲不接受她离开家,当她想要,并有男朋友。 与独立的母亲,谁在工作,并为她买了第一台相机,父亲也不接受她离开家。她和她一起打架,因为她迟到回家后,她花了一天在Enfoco学习和工作 - excerpt_original: Um ano atrás, em agosto de 2025, mais precisamente no dia 7, a fotógrafa Rosa Gauditano nos deixou. Ela tinha 70 anos. Eu conheci a Rosa há exatos 10 anos, em 2016. Eu e o Eduardo Costa fomos até a casa em que ela morava, na zona oeste de São Paulo, para fazer uma entrevista.…
translated_excerpt_zh: 一年前,2025年8月,更准确地说,7日,摄影师罗莎·加迪塔诺离开了我们,她70岁,我认识罗莎10年前,2016年,我和爱德华·科斯塔去了她住的房子,在西部的圣保罗地区,进行面试。

title_original: Awards Go To ‘Mayilaa,’ ‘The Gymnasts Of Fisherman Colony’ And More At Seattle’s Tasveer Film Festival
editorial_title_zh: 《Mayilaa》、《The Gymnasts Of Fisherman Colony》等作品在西雅图Tasveer电影节上斩获大奖
editorial_excerpt_zh: 西雅图Tasveer电影节日前落下帷幕，迎来其第21届活动的各项大奖揭晓。由森玛拉·安南（Semmalar Annam）执导的剧情片《Mayilaa》荣获最佳叙事长片评审团大奖。该片由P·梅洛迪·多卡斯（P. Melody Dorcas）、吉塔·凯拉萨姆（Geetha Kailasam）、舒达·科迪（Shudar Kodi）……

article_text:
The Tasveer Film Festival in Seattle has wrapped its 21 st edition with the announcement of awards in multiple categories.

Mayilaa , a drama directed by Semmalar Annam, won the Jury Award for Best Feature Narrative. The film starring P. Melody Dorcas, Geetha Kailasam, Shudar Kodi, and Sathya Maruthani tells a mother-daughter tale of “a novice saleswoman [who] travels South India to meet financial needs, despite having no sales experience.”

Mayilaa has also screened at Dharamshala International Film Festival in northern India, the Singapore International Film Festival, and International Film Festival Rotterdam in the Netherlands.

Related Stories

Emmy Winner Habiba Nosheen Flexes With 'The Gymnasts Of Fisherman Colony,' Inspiring Film From EPs Mariska Hargitay, Trish Adlesic, Malala Yousafzai

SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland's Contract With Updated Title

The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony , directed by Habiba Nosheen, won the Jury Award for Best Feature Documentary. The film centers on young women pursuing gymnastics in an area of Pakistan where such an athletic activity is uncommon for girls. As Deadline reported earlier this month , the documentary is executive produced by Mariska Hargitay, Trish Adlesic, and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Malala Yousafzai. Hargitay noted, “When we first learned about these young girls and their lives from director Habiba Nosheen, my producing partner, Trish Adlesic, and I knew we wanted to help ensure that their story would reach audiences around the world.”

Watch on Deadline

The Jury Award for Best Short went to The Last Glance , directed by Kamran Faiq and starring Adnan Shah Tipu and Areej Ayub Hussain.

Tasveer, which ran from October 13–18, showcased 136 films from 16 countries across more than 25 languages, including 20 World Premieres, 4 North American Premieres, and 4 U.S. Premieres. The festival notes, “The 2026 program included powerful storytelling by female directors, groundbreaking animation, an impressive slate of sports-centric cinema, and one of the festival’s strongest LGBTQ+ lineups to date.”

“Each film in this year’s lineup came to us carrying someone’s whole world,” noted Tasveer Executive Director Rita Meher. “Our role is to welcome it home, with a stage, a room full of industry, and real opportunities to go further. Watching filmmakers meet their audience and the people who can champion their work is exactly why we do this.”

Juried award winners were selected by a panel including Jury Lead Aparna Purohit (CEO of Aamir Khan Productions); James Longley (two-time Academy Award-nominated documentary filmmaker); Nekisa Cooper (former Head of Content at MasterClass, and president of the board of directors at Chicken & Egg Films), and Warren Etheredge (producer, film educator at the University of Washington, and co-founder of the Walla Walla Movie Crush).

“Some stories move us through their intimacy; others through their reflection of the world around us,” commented Jury Lead Aparna Purohit. “The films we considered at Tasveer did both, confronting the socio-political realities of our time with courage, sensitivity and remarkable cinematic vision.

“As Head of the Jury, it was a privilege and responsibility to engage with such a rich range of perspectives. I was deeply moved by the filmmakers’ honesty, diversity and ambition, and grateful to my fellow jurors for the thoughtful, open conversations that shaped our deliberations. I am delighted that Tasveer continues to give South Asian stories a platform to cross borders and resonate with audiences and communities worldwide. This experience reaffirmed why cinema matters: it reflects our world, challenges our assumptions and brings us closer to lives beyond our own, fostering greater empathy.”

The third annual Tasveer Film Market, “North America’s only industry platform dedicated to South Asian and diasporic cinema,” distributed $170,000 in awards across three competitive pitch events.

In its seventh year, the Tasveer Film Fund awarded $35,000 each to four original short film projects:

The Blue House – Red Reddy

Friendforhire.com – Nishanth R

Ghusl – Ambarien Alqadar

Planned Parenthood – Rahul Chaturvedi

The closing ceremony featured the announcement of the following award winners:

Jury Awards

Best Short: The Last Glance

Best Feature Narrative: Mayilaa

Best Feature Documentary: The Gymnasts of Fisherman Colony

Audience Choice Awards

Best Documentary Short: Salam Shalom

Best Documentary Feature: 49-51

Best Narrative Short: We Were Here

"text": "在项目《植物奥德赛》（Odyssée végétale）中，Sophie Zénon围绕时间性、缺席中的在场以及人类与非人类生存脆弱性等主题展开创作。她还探索了记忆、流亡和身份的内在动力。她的实践孕育出有机、充满活力且富有诗意的作品。她的项目邀请我们所有人去探索瓜德罗普岛和马提尼克岛的风光与奢华花园，摄影师对这些地方有着极深的感触。这是一部真正的作品，她通过移民的视角让植物与人类共存。「在我的作品中，处于不同形态中的植物（树木、植物、花卉、根茎）构成了一条贯穿始终的主线。它不仅是一个装饰性母题，更是进行更深层次的历史、生态与哲学思考及投入的场所，开启了构建新叙事、通往想象与感性感知空间的道路，」她在项目介绍中解释道。", glacières）。他的工作如同一次调查，他通过各种摄影技术和方法来进行。他利用模拟实验和科学工具来研究我们周围的事物。他的挑战在于审视我们周围那些贴近的事物，而不是望向遥远的地平线。Alain Nzuzi Polo通过《不可言说的考古学》（L’archéologie de
